lines.text: Separate a mixture → use the property that differs: filter off an insoluble solid, evaporate to recover a dissolved solid, recrystallize to purify one, distil to keep a liquid (fractional for close boiling points), paper chromatography for dyes ({{lesson:1.1}})
Protons, neutrons and electrons from $\ce{^{A}_{Z}X}$ → protons $= Z$, neutrons $= A - Z$, electrons $= Z$ minus the charge ({{lesson:1.2}})
$A_\text{r}$ from isotope masses and abundances → weighted mean, $\frac{\sum(\text{mass} \times \%)}{100}$; for an unknown abundance, call it $x$ and the other $100 - x$ ({{lesson:1.2}})
$A_\text{r}$ from a mass spectrum → $\frac{\sum(m/z \times \text{height})}{\sum \text{heights}}$; divide by 100 only when the heights total 100 ({{lesson:1.2}})
Photon energy, or the gap between two levels, from a wavelength → $\lambda$ in m, $f = \frac{c}{\lambda}$, then $E = hf$ ({{lesson:1.3}})

Electron configuration up to $Z = 36$ → fill 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p, singly before pairing; Cr is $\mathrm{[Ar]\,4s^{1}\,3d^{5}}$ and Cu $\mathrm{[Ar]\,4s^{1}\,3d^{10}}$; a d-block positive ion loses 4s before 3d ({{lesson:1.4}})
First ionization energy from a convergence limit → $E = hf$ (find $f = \frac{c}{\lambda}$ first for a wavelength), $\times N_\text{A}$, $\div 1000$ for $\pu{kJ mol-1}$ ({{lesson:1.5}})
Group of a main-group element from successive ionization energies → find the first very large jump; 1 or 2 electrons before it means group 1 or 2, 3 to 8 means add 10 ({{lesson:1.5}})

Link mass, number of particles and a solution → go through moles: $n = \frac{m}{M}$, $N = nN_\text{A}$, $n = CV$ with $V$ in $\pu{dm3}$; for a dilution $C_1V_1 = C_2V_2$ ({{lesson:1.6}}, {{lesson:1.8}})

Empirical formula from percentages or masses → divide each mass by $A_\text{r}$, divide by the smallest, make whole numbers; molecular formula → multiply by $n = \frac{M}{M(\text{empirical formula})}$ ({{lesson:1.7}})
Volumes of gases that react or form, all at the same $T$ and $P$ → volume ratio $=$ coefficient ratio, gases only ({{lesson:1.8}})

Gas amount, volume or molar mass → at STP $n = \frac{V}{V_\text{m}}$ with $\pu{22.7 dm3 mol-1}$; otherwise $PV = nRT$ in Pa, $\pu{m3}$ and K, with $M = \frac{mRT}{PV}$; a fixed amount changing conditions → $\frac{P_1V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2V_2}{T_2}$, $T$ in kelvin ({{lesson:1.9}})
